title: Mastery of Corneal Astigmatism: From Diagnostics to Surgical Correction
summary: Corneal astigmatism, defined by non-spherical corneal curvature, necessitates precise diagnostic mapping and evidence-based surgical intervention. This guide navigates the path from topometric analysis to advanced refractive correction techniques.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Corneal astigmatism occurs when the corneal surface is toroidal rather than spherical. It is defined as a refractive state where the eye's refractive power varies across different meridians, resulting in two focal lines instead of a single point (Sturm's Conoid). Pathophysiology typically relates to the anterior corneal surface curvature, though posterior corneal surface contribution (PCC) is critical in modern surgical planning.

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Suspect Ectasia

content.explanation: Topography check, Orientation alignment (0-180), Rotation risks, IOL stability, Capsular bag integrity.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always account for Posterior Corneal Astigmatism (PCA) using the Barrett Toric Calculator.
Surgically Induced Astigmatism (SIA) at the incision site should be calculated via vector analysis.
For cataract surgery: Consider LRI for < 1.0D and Toric IOL for > 1.0D of corneal astigmatism.
Epithelial thickness mapping is the 'gold standard' for detecting early Keratoconus.
